source.raw_text: [Music] the purpose of the x-axis way cover is to protect the ball screw and guideways from chips coolant and any other debris inside the machine enclosure in this video we're gonna look at replacing the x-axis way covers on your mill and do some troubleshooting along the way if the bolts that holds the way cover rails to the castings are loose the way covers make popping noise when they are moving this will eventually damage the plastic tabs that slide on the rails this in turn will cause a section of the way covers to separate and leak so as soon as the way covers start making that popping noise pulled away covers back and inspect the rails for loose fasteners tighten the fasteners and apply a thin coat of red-eye grease to the guide rails to prevent that issue in the future in a normal machine operation weight covers are lubricated by the coolant it is critical to maintain the correct coolant concentration so use a refractometer to check the coolant concentration now if you have to cut parts without flood cooling make sure that you lubricate all the way covers with a lightweight oil fully extended way covers and spray an even coat of lightweight oil on the way covers if you continue to run the machine without lubricant the rubber seals will break down prematurely now let's review how to replace the entire way cover and also we look at replacing just the wiper if they're the only thing that's damaged if the way cover wipers are damaged luckily these can be changed out on their own we'll review the old style and the new style x-axis Way covers starting with the new style way covers first jog the x-axis all the way to the end of travel he stopped the machine remove the x-axis way cover turn it over and remove each section wipe away any excess grease locate and remove the small Phillips screw with a flathead screwdriver the retaining strip towards the opposite end and remove it from the standoffs remove the damaged wiper cut the new wiper to the exact length and verify the holes are aligned with the new wiper cut clean up the way cover and apply a light coat of red-eye grease to the wiper and install the wiper correctly back on the way cover install the retainer and make sure the retainer capture all the standoffs with one hand apply a little pressure to the retainer and use a flathead screwdriver to slide the retainer into the locking position on the standoff once all the wipers are installed put the sections back together now for the old-style way covers the wiper replacement process is slightly different use a flathead screwdriver to remove the way cover wiper and clean the channel out with the sections apart that was a good time to take care of any dent in the way covers now cut the replacement wiper to the same length as the original one you just removed apply a light coat of redeye agrees to each replacement wiper and then install them using a mallet to tap the wiper firmly into the slot finally install each section back together at this point the steps are the same whether you're reinstalling their existing x-axis way covers or you're installing some new ones remove any chips and debris from the linear guides remove the used gasket and sealant from the table mounting surface and clean it apply a thin coat of red-eye grease to the way cover guide bar and install the way cover over the guide bars attach the way cover and panel to the way cover bracket with the fasteners fully extend away cover one leaf at a time to make sure the section don't separate with the largest leaf of the way cover away from the table put a bead of RTV silicone followed by the new gasket on the face of the way cover attach the way cover to the table install the fasteners and wipe away any excess silicone from the table release the e stop and press reset a couple times to clear the alarms apply a light coat of oil to all sections of the way cover and jog the x-axis slowly to make sure the way cover does not bind follow the same process for the other side in August 2013 the VF one through VF five machines change to a new revision of x-axis Way covers the new way covers have a slightly different mounting configuration they attach directly to the guide bars this provide a stronger support for the way covers some slight modification may be needed for machines that was built when this was first introduced for this the following tools are required a way cover kit a number twenty one drill bit 1032 tap a tube of black RTV silicone a red eye grease cartridge and a scraper let's get into it jog the x-axis all the way to the opposite end of travel put the machine in e-stop remove the all x-axis way cover and L bracket locate the two holes on the way cover mounting bar if the holes are not drilled all the way through use the number twenty one drill bit and break it through then use a 1032 tap to tap the holes all the way now with the holes drill in tapped in the guide bars will remove the guide bars from the machine and install them in the way cover and then install the way cover and guide bars on the machine as an assembly now check the transition between the way cover guide bar and the casting for smoothness if the surface is not smooth the tabs on the bottom of the way covers will get caught and damaged away covers once that's completed reinstall the way covers jog the axis around a couple of times to make sure it's not binding this process is now completed for more information or to order parts we've used in this service video visit Haas CNC comm and thanks for watching

look at replacing the x-axis way covers on your mill and do some troubleshooting along the way if the bolts that holds the way cover rails to the castings are loose the way covers make popping noise when they are moving this will eventually damage the plastic tabs that slide on the rails this in turn will cause a section of the way covers to separate and leak so as soon as the way covers start making that popping noise pulled away covers back and inspect the rails for loose fasteners tighten the fasteners and apply a thin coat of red-eye grease to the guide rails to prevent that issue in the future in a normal machine operation weight covers are lubricated by the coolant it is critical to maintain the correct coolant concentration so use a refractometer to check the coolant concentration now if you have to cut parts without flood cooling make sure that you lubricate all the way covers with a lightweight oil fully extended way covers and spray an even coat of lightweight oil on the way covers if you continue to run the machine without lubricant the rubber seals will break down prematurely now let's review how to replace the entire way cover and also we look at replacing just the wiper if they're the only thing that's damaged if the way cover wipers are damaged luckily these can be changed out on their own we'll review the old style and the new style x-axis Way covers starting with the new style way covers first jog the x-axis all the way to the end of travel he stopped the machine remove the x-axis way cover turn it over and remove each section wipe away any excess grease locate and remove the small Phillips screw with a flathead screwdriver the retaining strip towards the opposite end and remove it from the standoffs remove the damaged wiper cut the new wiper to the exact length and verify the holes are aligned with the new wiper cut clean up the way cover and apply a light coat of red-eye grease to the wiper and install the wiper correctly back on the way cover install the retainer and make sure the retainer capture all the standoffs with one hand apply a little pressure to the retainer and use a flathead screwdriver to slide the retainer into the locking position on the standoff once all the wipers are installed put the sections back together now for the old-style way covers the wiper replacement process is slightly different use a flathead screwdriver to remove the way cover wiper and clean the channel out with the sections apart that was a good time to take care of any dent in the way covers now cut the replacement wiper to the same length as the original one you just removed apply a light coat of redeye agrees to each replacement wiper and then install them using a mallet to tap the wiper firmly into the slot finally install each section back together at this point the steps are the same whether you're reinstalling their existing x-axis way covers or you're installing some new ones remove any chips and debris from the linear guides remove the used gasket and sealant from the table mounting surface and clean it apply a thin coat of red-eye grease to the way cover guide bar and install the way cover over the guide bars attach the way cover and panel to the way cover bracket with the fasteners fully extend away cover one leaf at a time to make sure the section don't separate with the largest leaf of the way cover away from the table put a bead of RTV silicone followed by the new gasket on the face of the way cover attach the way cover to the table install the fasteners and wipe away any excess silicone from the table release the e stop and press reset a couple times to clear the alarms apply a light coat of oil to all sections of the way cover and jog the x-axis slowly to make sure the way cover does not bind follow the same process for the other side in August 2013 the VF one through VF five machines change to a new revision of x-axis Way covers the new way covers have a slightly different mounting configuration they attach directly to the guide bars this provide a stronger support for the way covers some slight modification may be needed for machines that was built when this was first introduced for this the following tools are required a way cover kit a number twenty one drill bit 1032 tap a tube of black RTV silicone a red eye grease cartridge and a scraper let's get into it jog the x-axis all the way to the opposite end of travel put the machine in e-stop remove the all x-axis way cover and L bracket locate the two holes on the way cover mounting bar if the holes are not drilled all the way through use the number twenty one drill bit and break it through then use a 1032 tap to tap the holes all the way now with the holes drill in tapped in the guide bars will remove the guide bars from the machine and install them in the way cover and then install the way cover and guide bars on the machine as an assembly now check the transition between the way cover guide bar and the casting for smoothness if the surface is not smooth the tabs on the bottom of the way covers will get caught and damaged away covers once that's completed reinstall the way covers jog the axis around a couple of times to make sure it's not binding this process is now completed for more information or to order parts we've used in this service video visit Haas CNC comm and thanks for watching
